definition: A paid angle as produced by produce-paid-angles: the strategic stance an ad takes, encoded as angle.json (schema angle/1.6, the four coordinates incl. the negative).
target: An angle takes a falsifiable stance against a named negative. It names what it stands against (the negative coordinate: competitor, category belief, status quo, substitute, diy, do-nothing), makes a claim specific enough that it could be wrong, and could not be pasted onto any other brand. It traces to a spectrum cell, so it is encoded knowledge, not a fresh invention.

criteria.pass: Names the specific thing the angle pushes against (the 4th coordinate): a competitor, a category belief, the status quo, a substitute, DIY, or doing nothing.
criteria.fail: All upside, no enemy. The angle floats with nothing to react against, so it persuades no one already content.

criteria.pass: Makes a claim a skeptic could contest. There is a reader for whom this is the wrong angle.
criteria.fail: A truism ('quality you can trust', 'feel your best') that no one disputes and no one is moved by.

criteria.pass: Anchored to this product's mechanism and this audience's tension. Swap the brand name and it breaks.
criteria.fail: Could be any brand in the category. Passes the 'rename test' unchanged.

criteria.pass: References the spectrum cell / awareness-sophistication coordinate it derives from. Encoded, not freelanced.
criteria.fail: No trace to the brand's strategic spectrum. Invented in isolation.
